checkpoint.measure: Score share against fixed practice opponents (0.5 = even)
checkpoint.tier_note: No L1 / L3 panels: this card's opponents are REF / TRUTH / TWIN, and the main curve already includes its strong level (TRUTH).

names: Head camera: keeping the shuttle in view

skills.name: Keeps a high shuttle in view
skills.real: One head camera. When a high shot passes overhead the robot leans back and turns so the shuttle stays in the image long enough to fit its flight. Real players gain time by seeing the shuttle early.
skills.measure: Checkpoint Evaluation replay: head camera pose + shuttle position; per high shot (apex ≥ 2.5 m) the time it is inside the camera frustum, median per match. Gate: ≥ 3 high shots.

skills.name: Racket reaches the flight (predicting it under drag)
skills.real: A shuttle loses half its speed every 3.35 m, so a drag-free parabola misses. Only a drag-aware prediction puts the racket head on the flight.
skills.measure: Checkpoint Evaluation replay: closest racket-head-to-shuttle distance while the shuttle is the program's to play; share of incoming shots under 20 cm. Scenario recv: the same reading on pinned serves.
skills.line: ≥ 50 % of incoming shots in 2/3 of matches (gate ≥ 5)

skills.name: Gets to the contact point
skills.real: The Engineer trains its own walking. A shot out of reach is lost within 0.4 s; deep-corner serves land 0.8-1.1 m behind the stance.
skills.measure: Match: foot travel inside a rally from replay (placements excluded), median per rally. Scenario reach: for each receive the robot is placed 0.55 m in front of and 0.25 m inside its spot and the opponent serves its hardest-to-reach deep corner; the match record whether the program touched the shuttle.
skills.line: Match: ≥ 0.3 m per rally (2/3 of matches); scenario: touches ≥ 50 % of the serves

skills.name: Stays stable while swinging (receiving after a push)
skills.real: A stroke is a whole-body action held up by the legs. Stable means taking a knock, from contact or the swing's own reaction, and still standing and hitting.
skills.measure: Scenario push: the opponent serves every point; 50 ms after each serve leaves the racket the program's pelvis gets a 1.2 m/s sideways push (alternating; 0.4 m/s knocked nobody down). Read from the match record: a fall within the point, and whether the program touched the shuttle.
skills.line: No fall in ≥ 2/3 of pushed points; gate: the same program touches ≥ 30 % of the serves in recv (it plays)

skills.name: Feet still before the serve
skills.real: BWF Law 9.1.4: both players' feet stay put until the serve is delivered; over 3 cm is a fault.
skills.measure: the match record: points lost to an own ':moved' fault / all points. Gate: ≥ 20 own swings (replay).

skills.name: Returns the shuttle (contact accuracy and timing)
skills.real: At the joint layer the racket head reaches the contact point at the right moment with the right face and speed, so the shuttle clears the net and lands in.
skills.measure: the match record: own non-serve hits / opponent hits, pooled over a checkpoint's Checkpoint Evaluations.

skills.name: Receives the serve
skills.real: Receiving is relatively easy in real badminton; here the chain from seeing the toss to the swing is the robot's main bottleneck. Every legal serve is returnable from some stance.
skills.measure: Match: share of opponent-serve points in which the program touches the shuttle at least once. Scenario recv: the opponent serves every point with one pinned middle serve per court; share touched.

skills.name: Reacts in time (real-time timing)
skills.real: ETH's badminton robot needs about 0.37 s from the opponent's hit to its swing. Plans 200 ms late or more clearly lose points.
skills.measure: Checkpoint Evaluation replay: time from the opponent's hit to the racket head starting to move, median per match; no response is censored.

skills.name: Serves legally
skills.real: Toss, contact below 1.15 m, land in the diagonal service court. Hard-to-return serving is secondary (main's reference returns the hardest legal serve).
skills.measure: Scenario serve: the program serves every point; share of serves with no serve_fault in the match record. In matches the same reading (serves_legal / serves).

off.name: Placement and reading the opponent (secondary)
off.why: The card has only match-result evidence (always the same corner -0.11). Match results belong to the growth curve.

off.name: Engineering, Adaptive
off.why: Not declared on the badminton card. How the agent builds and changes the system is read across checkpoints (the growth curve).

open_questions: Whether scenario readings and match re-test readings count equally on the curve (now: where a skill has both, failing either counts as failing).
The proposed pass lines (scenario 50 % touched, push 90 % no fall, getup 2/3 within 20 s, search 2/3 within 5 s, loose 2/3 within 1 s). The reference's readings are in each results table.
Whether the scenario variants join GROWTH's re-test queue (now a separate docker runner; the world patch is recorded in every result).

notes.challenge: A humanoid with a racket and one head depth camera. The program keeps the shuttle in view, predicts its flight under real drag and gets the racket to the contact point while staying balanced.

achieved.text: Untouched serves decided most points, but in BAD3-F18 (Gemini 4 Argon against GPT-6 Astra) 9 of 18 points had a third contact, among them a four-contact rally.
Receiving in the Championship: GPT-6 Astra touched 19 of 25 receives and Gemini 18 of 24; Claude Opus 5.5 15 of 50, Kimi 3.1 Pro 5 of 47, DeepSeek 2 of 43, GLM 0 of 45.
Opus predicted the shuttle to within 1 to 9 cm and still missed six interceptions with its racket centre 10 to 31 cm from the shuttle.

Opus noticed that Kimi's serve was the same on each court, replayed it in practice and came back from 0:6 to 11:6. In their rematch Kimi served the serves its match video showed Opus falling under, and won 11:6 on 10 of 11 own serves.

GPT-6 Astra: Trained a walking policy and kept it out of the match ("Do not enable movement just because a saved model exists"); its serve contact sat a median 3.5 mm from the racket centre.
Gemini 4 Argon: Played without the GPU on top of the practice simulator's own perception and stroke code, and studied its earlier match against Opus from the library video and logs.

interface.sees: Two head cameras, the G1's stereo pair (480 × 360 each, a new frame every 10 ms), its own joints, balance sensor, position and racket pose, the sound of serves and hits, and the score. No shuttle coordinates.
interface.controls: Targets for all 29 joints in a plan of up to 300 rows of 10 ms, with optional speeds, torques, stiffness and damping; plus a shuttle toss to serve and where to stand to receive. Real time.
interface.moment: Final, Gemini 4 Argon v GPT-6 Astra, match point with Astra ahead 10–7, 1:15 in the replay. Gemini's shot is coming over the net to Astra's robot (ringed), 0.28 s before Astra plays it; Gemini's next shot lands out and Astra wins 11–7.
details: Cameras: the G1's two head cameras, 5 cm apart, fixed to the trunk and tilted 23° up, 480 × 360 each with a 58° vertical field of view, side by side in one image. A new frame every 10 ms; the newest a program can fetch is 20 ms old, with both cameras' poses.
Not given: where the shuttle is. It is drawn as an orange cork with a white skirt, and the program finds it in the images. A shuttle high above the robot or low at its feet is out of view.

Own robot: pelvis position, heading and trunk tilt, velocity, all 29 joint angles and speeds, the pelvis IMU, the targets and gains in force, whether it is down, and the racket's position, face direction and speed.
Referee: score, whose serve, the serve's phase and deadlines, whether the shuttle is coming to it, and what it heard: serves and hits, whose, and how long ago.

Command: a plan of joint targets for legs, waist and arms, one row per 10 ms step, up to 300 rows, with optional velocities, feed-forward torques and gains. Rows are clipped at the joint ranges and speed limits; the joint controller runs every 2 ms through the motors' torque–speed curves.
Serve and receive: a shuttle toss within 3 s of the serve opening, struck below 1.15 m by the program's own stroke; a stance command picks where the robot stands to receive.
No ready-made skills: no walking policy, balance, get-up or stroke planner. With the default gains alone the robot sinks and falls in about 1.5 s.
Timing: a control step every 10 ms; the world runs at real speed and never waits; a command acts at the next step, one command in flight. After each point the world pauses for reviews.
Rules: BWF badminton on a court at 0.4 of full size, one game to 11 (lead of 2, at most 15). No bounce: the shuttle must be hit before it lands.
Before the match: 2 hours of preparation with a full practice copy of the court, a practice opponent and a GPU training kit (half an RTX PRO 6000).
